title: Spain SMB Quickstart: Market Activation & Messaging
content:
Purpose:
This working brief is a focused go-to-market and enablement package for an initial Spain SMB activation of Redwood Inference features (hosted API + flexible dedicated options + Spanish language support). It is intended for sales, solutions engineering, growth, and partner teams to use for a 6-week pilot push with local VAR partners and developer meetups.

Why Spain, why now:
- Market signals: high usage of cloud SaaS among Spanish SMBs, rising interest in generative automation for customer support and content localization.
- Competitive window: Many customers currently prototype on general cloud AI endpoints but struggle with predictable token costs and regional latency.
- Regulatory tailwinds: Local customers appreciate EU-region options and straightforward private deployment offers for customer PII.

Top-level positioning (1-liner):
Redwood Inference gives Spanish development teams predictable, low-latency LLM inference—across hosted, reserved, and private deployments—so product teams can ship conversational and automation features without building or overpaying for infrastructure.

Messaging pillars (short):
1) Production economics: predictable per-unit costs and tools to lower unit spend (batching, caching, quantization guides).
2) Regional performance: EU-region latency and deployment flexibility (VPC/private).
3) Dev-first experience: clear SDKs, quickstart templates for Spanish-language prompts and evals.
4) Reliability & fallbacks: multi-variant routing and automatic degradation policies for business-critical flows.

Target personas (priority order):
- Product/Engineering lead at SMB (SaaS, e-commerce, marketplaces): cares about time-to-value, SDKs, and cost predictability.
- Head of Customer Support / Ops: wants reliable Spanish-language assistants and data controls.
- Platform/DevOps at fast-growing startups: needs reserved capacity or private deployment options and observability.
- Solutions partner/System integrator (local MSPs): wants clear onboarding playbooks and demo-apps.

Key benefits (talking points for demos):
- Lower token cost per request through recommended batching + KV caching; show 20–50% cost reduction examples for chat workloads.
- Sub-100ms regional tail latency for short-context chat (demo with Madrid region in sandbox).
- Canary rollouts and A/B routing mean you can validate a new model version without customer-visible regressions.
- Easy Spanish prompt templates and out-of-the-box evals to detect hallucination/regression in localized text.

Competitive snapshot (notes for SDRs / AE rebuttals):
- Cloud AI endpoints (major hyperscalers): stronger model breadth but weaker unit economics for small to medium sustained workloads; less opinionated serving optimizations (e.g., continuous batching) and limited rollout primitives.
- Hosted LLM API competitors: similar simplicity, but Redwood differentiates with dedicated capacity and private deploys that are easier to purchase for SMBs via partners.
- Self-hosted open-source stacks: lower raw license cost but high ops burden; Redwood sells predictable, developer-friendly ownership with lower TCO when ops overhead is included.

Common objections + short counters (sales snippets):
- "We can run models ourselves cheaper." -> "If your team builds a custom stack you’ll trade engineering time for ops complexity. Redwood reduces total cost by automating batching/caching and offering reserved capacity with clear cost forecasts."
- "We need Spanish data controls." -> "Private deployment and VPC options let you keep control of keys and logs while using the same control plane and SDKs as hosted users."

Localized announcement copy (external, short):
EN: "Redwood Inference: now ready for Spanish teams—predictable inference costs, regional performance, and private deployment options to bring generative features to production."
ES: "Redwood Inference ya disponible para equipos en España: costes predecibles, latencia regional y opciones de despliegue privado para poner funciones generativas en producción."

Internal launch Slack / email (one-liner for org):
"Heads-up: Spain SMB quickstart goes live for pilot customers next week. Sales kit, pricing sheets, and partner playbook are in the GTM folder — reach out to Martina Ruiz for bespoke demos or partner intros."

Sales enablement checklist (minimum viable):
- One-pager (EN + ES) that maps features to SMB use-cases (support automation, smart replies, content localization).
- Two demo flows: 1) Spanish support assistant (chat + knowledge retrieval); 2) customer email summarization/response generator.
- Pricing cheat sheet for 1, 3, and 12-month commitments (hosted vs dedicated).
- Solutions engineering runbook for private deployments (network checklist, KMS notes, logs retention).
- Partner onboarding slides + 30-minute partner kickoff template.

Product/SE playbook highlights (technical talking points):
- Recommended models for Spanish: (1) small low-latency variant for short-turn chat, (2) mid-sized for longer generation and summarization. Provide quick perf numbers and cost tradeoffs.
- Batching & cache defaults: suggest session KV caching for chat with 3-turn warm-up policy; show perf delta in bench notes.
- Rollout strategy: use canary 5% traffic -> monitor latency/error/quality -> expand. Include fallback to smaller variant if latency SLO breaches.

Launch timeline (6-week sprint):
Week 0: finalize localized one-pager, pricing options, and partner list.
Week 1–2: SE demo builds, testbeds created (Spanish corpora), and partner kickoff.
Week 3: soft pilot with 3 SMBs + SE support.
Week 4: gather metrics, iterate prompts/quant profiles.
Week 5: expand to 10 customers and begin paid upsell conversations.
Week 6: public regional announcement and partner webinar.

Success metrics (early signals):
- 10 pilot signups in first 4 weeks.
- Average token spend predictability within +/-10% of forecast for pilots.
- Two customer stories/demo videos for website within 8 weeks.
- NPS >= 60 for pilot participants on initial setup & docs.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Low demo lift for Spanish language quality -> Mitigate: add curated Spanish prompt sets and run short in-house evals before demos.
- Partner friction on private deployments -> Mitigate: prepare a one-click onboarding checklist and assign an SE buddy.

Assets to produce (priority order):
1) Localized one-pager (ES + EN)
2) Two demo apps + reproducible scripts
3) Pricing cheat sheet + reservation examples
4) SE runbook for private/VPC
5) Short partner playbook + partner pitch deck

Appendix: sample objection scripts for AE (short bullets):
- "Model quality" -> "We provide model-performance profiles and pre-built evals; we’ll run your prompt set in advance and show objective deltas."
- "Cost concerns" -> "We can model your current token profile and show an optimized configuration (batching + reserved) that reduces cost per effective response."

Next steps (action owners):
- Martina Ruiz: finalize ES one-pager and coordinate partner list (due 2025-02-24).
- Liam Patel: build Spanish support demo infra and perf notes (due 2025-02-28).
- Sofia Nguyen: pricing scenarios and reservation SKUs (due 2025-02-27).
- Carlos Álvarez: partner kickoff invites and co-sell ops (due 2025-02-26).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working activation pack; content is intentionally concise to allow SEs and AEs to adapt to customer language. Please add links to repos or Confluence pages in the linked_artifacts list above.

-- End of brief --
